{{Short description|Hierarchy of formulas in set theory}}

In [[set theory]] and [[mathematical logic]], the '''Lévy hierarchy''', introduced by [[Azriel Lévy]] in 1965, is a hierarchy of formulas in the [[formal language]] of the [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory]] (ZFC), which is typically called just the language of set theory. This is analogous to the [[arithmetical hierarchy]], which provides a similar classification for sentences of the language of [[Peano arithmetic|arithmetic]].

==Definitions==

In the language of set theory, [[atomic formula]]s are of the form x = y or x ∈ y, standing for [[Equality (mathematics)|equality]] and [[set membership]] predicates, respectively.

The first level of the Lévy hierarchy is defined as containing only formulas with no [[Bounded quantifier|unbounded quantifiers]] and is denoted by <math>\Delta_0=\Sigma_0=\Pi_0</math>.<ref name="Walicki">Walicki, Michal (2012). ''Mathematical Logic'', p. 225. World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd. {{isbn|9789814343862}}</ref> The next levels are given by finding a formula in [[prenex normal form]] that is provably equivalent over ZFC, and counting the number of alternations of [[quantifier (logic)|quantifier]]s:<ref name="Jech2006">T. Jech, 'Set Theory: The Third Millennium Edition, revised and expanded'. Springer Monographs in Mathematics (2006). ISBN 3-540-44085-2.</ref><sup>p.&nbsp;184</sup>

A formula <math>A</math> is called:<ref name="Walicki" /><ref>J. Baeten, [https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/12723/12723D.pdf Filters and ultrafilters over definable subsets over admissible ordinals] (1986). p.10</ref>

* <math>\Sigma_{i+1}</math> if <math>A</math> is equivalent to <math>\exists x_1 ... \exists x_n B</math> in ZFC, where <math>B</math> is <math>\Pi_i</math>
* <math>\Pi_{i+1}</math> if <math>A</math> is equivalent to <math>\forall x_1 ... \forall x_n B</math> in ZFC, where <math>B</math> is <math>\Sigma_i</math>
* If a formula is both <math>\Sigma_i</math> and <math>\Pi_i</math> form, it is called <math>\Delta_i</math>.

As a formula might have several different equivalent formulas in prenex normal form, it might belong to several different levels of the hierarchy. In this case, the lowest possible level is the level of the formula.{{citation needed|date=July 2023}}

Lévy's original notation was <math>\Sigma_i^\mathsf{ZFC}</math> (respectively <math>\Pi_i^\mathsf{ZFC}</math>) due to the provable logical equivalence,<ref name="Levy65">A. Lévy, 'A hierarchy of formulas in set theory' (1965), second edition</ref> strictly speaking the above levels should be referred to as <math>\Sigma_i^\mathsf{ZFC}</math> (respectively <math>\Pi_i^\mathsf{ZFC}</math>) to specify the theory in which the equivalence is carried out, however it is usually clear from context.<ref>K. Hauser, "Indescribable cardinals and elementary embeddings". [[Journal of Symbolic Logic]] vol. 56, iss. 2 (1991), pp.439--457.</ref><sup>pp.&nbsp;441–442</sup> Pohlers has defined <math>\Delta_1</math> in particular semantically, in which a formula is "<math>\Delta_1</math> in a structure <math>M</math>".<ref>W. Pohlers, ''Proof Theory: The First Step into Impredicativity'' (2009) (p.245)</ref>

The Lévy hierarchy is sometimes defined for other theories ''S''. In this case <math>\Sigma_i</math> and <math>\Pi_i</math> by themselves refer only to formulas that start with a sequence of quantifiers with at most ''i''−1 alternations,{{citation needed|date=July 2023}} and <math>\Sigma_i^S</math> and  <math>\Pi_i^S</math> refer to formulas equivalent to <math>\Sigma_i</math> and <math>\Pi_i</math> formulas in the language of the theory ''S''. So strictly speaking the levels <math>\Sigma_i</math> and <math>\Pi_i</math> of the Lévy hierarchy for ZFC defined above should be denoted by  <math>\Sigma^{\mathsf{ZFC}} _i</math> and  <math>\Pi^{\mathsf{ZFC}}_i</math>.

==Examples==
{{Prose|Examples|date=August 2026}}

===Σ<sub>0</sub>=Π<sub>0</sub>=Δ<sub>0</sub> formulas and concepts===
* x = {y, z}<ref name="Barwise75">[[Jon Barwise]], ''Admissible Sets and Structures''. Perspectives in Mathematical Logic (1975)</ref><sup>p.&nbsp;14</sup>
* x ⊆ y <ref name="Monk2011">D. Monk 2011, [https://web.archive.org/web/20111206123643/http://euclid.colorado.edu/~monkd/m6730/gradsets14.pdf Graduate Set Theory] (pp.168--170). Archived 2011-12-06</ref>
* ''x'' is a [[transitive set]]<ref name="Monk2011" />
* ''x'' is an [[Ordinal number|ordinal]], ''x'' is a [[limit ordinal]], ''x'' is a [[successor ordinal]]<ref name="Monk2011" />
* ''x'' is a finite ordinal<ref name="Monk2011" />
* The first infinite [[Ordinal number|ordinal]] ω <ref name="Monk2011" />
* ''x'' is an ordered pair. The first entry of the ordered pair ''x'' is ''a''. The second entry of the ordered pair ''x'' is ''b'' <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;14</sup>
* ''f'' is a function. ''x'' is the domain/range of the function ''f''. ''y'' is the value of ''f'' on ''x'' <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;14</sup>
* The [[Cartesian product]] of two sets.
* ''x'' is the union of ''y'' <ref name="Monk2011" />
* ''x'' is a member of the ''α''th level of Gödel's [[Constructible universe|L]]<ref>W. A. R. Weiss, [https://www.math.toronto.edu/weiss/Set_Theory.pdf An Introduction to Set Theory] (chapter 13). Accessed 2022-12-01</ref>
* ''R'' is a relation with domain/range/field ''a'' <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;14</sup>
* ''X'' is Hausdorff.

===Δ<sub>1</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* ''x'' is a [[well-founded relation]] on ''y'' <ref>K. J. Williams, [https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.03955.pdf Minimum models of second-order set theories] (2019, p.4). Accessed 2022 July 25.</ref>
* ''x'' is finite <ref name="Levy65" /><sup>p.15</sup>
* [[Ordinal addition]] and multiplication and exponentiation <ref>F. R. Drake, ''Set Theory: An Introduction to Large Cardinals'' (p.83). Accessed 1 July 2022.</ref>
* ''x'' has rank ''α'' <ref name="Kanamori2011">[[Akihiro Kanamori]], ''The Higher Infinite: Large Cardinals in Set Theory from Their Beginnings'' (p.5). Springer (2009)</ref>
* The rank (with respect to [[Constructible universe|Gödel's constructible universe]]) of a set <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;61</sup>
* The [[transitive closure]] of a set.
* The specifiability relation Sp(A) for a set A. <ref>F. R. Drake, ''Set Theory: An Introduction to Large Cardinals'' (p.127). Accessed 4 October 2024.</ref>

===Σ<sub>1</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* ''x'' is [[Countable set|countable]].
* |''X''|≤|''Y''|, |''X''|=|''Y''|.
* ''x'' is constructible.
* ''g'' is the restriction of the function ''f'' to ''a'' <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;23</sup>
* ''g'' is the image of ''f'' on ''a'' <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;23</sup>
* ''b'' is the successor ordinal of ''a'' <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;23</sup>
* The [[Mostowski collapse lemma|Mostowski collapse]] of <math>(x,\in)</math> <ref name="Barwise75" /><sup>p.&nbsp;29</sup>

===Π<sub>1</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* ''x'' is a [[cardinal number|cardinal]]
* ''x'' is a [[regular cardinal]]
* ''x'' is a [[limit cardinal]]
* ''x'' is an [[inaccessible cardinal]].
* ''x'' is the [[powerset]] of ''y''
* ''x'' is <math>V_{\alpha}</math>

===Δ<sub>2</sub>-formulas and concepts===

*''κ'' is ''γ''-[[supercompact cardinal|supercompact]]

===Σ<sub>2</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* the [[continuum hypothesis]] 
* there exists an [[inaccessible cardinal]]
* there exists a [[measurable cardinal]]
* ''κ'' is an ''n''-[[huge cardinal]]

===Π<sub>2</sub>-formulas and concepts===
* The axiom of choice<ref name="Levy71">Azriel Lévy, "On the logical complexity of several axioms of set theory" (1971). Appearing in ''Axiomatic Set Theory: Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics, vol. 13 part 1'', pp.219--230</ref>
* The generalized continuum hypothesis<ref name="Levy71" />
* The [[axiom of constructibility]]: ''[[Von Neumann universe|V]]'' = ''[[Constructible universe|L]]''<ref name="Levy71" />

===Δ<sub>3</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* ''κ'' is an [[measurable cardinal]]

===Σ<sub>3</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* there exists a [[supercompact cardinal]]

===Π<sub>3</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* ''κ'' is an [[extendible cardinal]]

===Σ<sub>4</sub>-formulas and concepts===

* there exists an [[extendible cardinal]]

== Properties ==
Let <math>n\geq 1</math>. The Lévy hierarchy has the following properties:<ref name="Jech2006" /><sup>p.&nbsp;184</sup>
* If <math>\phi</math> is <math>\Sigma_n</math>, then <math>\lnot\phi</math> is <math>\Pi_n</math>.
* If <math>\phi</math> is <math>\Pi_n</math>, then <math>\lnot\phi</math> is <math>\Sigma_n</math>.
* If <math>\phi</math> and <math>\psi</math> are <math>\Sigma_n</math>, then <math>\exists x\phi</math>, <math>\phi\land\psi</math>, <math>\phi\lor\psi</math>, <math>\exists(x\in z)\phi</math>, and <math>\forall(x\in z)\phi</math> are all <math>\Sigma_n</math>.
* If <math>\phi</math> and <math>\psi</math> are <math>\Pi_n</math>, then <math>\forall x\phi</math>, <math>\phi\land\psi</math>, <math>\phi\lor\psi</math>, <math>\exists(x\in z)\phi</math>, and <math>\forall(x\in z)\phi</math> are all <math>\Pi_n</math>.
* If <math>\phi</math> is <math>\Sigma_n</math> and <math>\psi</math> is <math>\Pi_n</math>, then <math>\phi\implies\psi</math> is <math>\Pi_n</math>.
* If <math>\phi</math> is <math>\Pi_n</math> and <math>\psi</math> is <math>\Sigma_n</math>, then <math>\phi\implies\psi</math> is <math>\Sigma_n</math>.

Devlin p.&nbsp;29
